text: Studying for finals late at night, I need calm music that won't distract me.

summary:
I'm narrowing down the playlist options and leaning toward the classical picks, since instrumental tracks like these are unlikely to be distracting. I'll keep the jazz option as a fallback, but I'm settling on classical.

I'm also looking at 3AM Thoughts, which seems to be bedroom pop and may have vocals, so I'll skip it.

I'm checking which sources are missing: there are no classical, Elena Varga, or Orbit Bloom notes, and no lofi genre note either. That's fine, so I'll go with ambient, bossa nova, and the artist notes I do have.

input.title: Quiet Hours Before Finals

picks.why: A steady, focused lo-fi loop that settles your mind into the first stretch of reading.
Soft library rain and a gentle beat, made by students for exactly this late-night desk.
Low-energy ambient texture that fades into the background while you work through problem sets.
Hushed nylon-string guitar from a Rio window, calm enough to keep your attention on your notes.
A slow, quiet classical piece to close the session as your eyes start getting heavy.

input.story: Brian Eno coined "ambient music" for sound you can either listen to closely or ignore, and that idea links these picks. LoRoom makes loops meant to sit behind study sessions. Paper Lanterns, a self-released duo, samples rain recorded outside their university library. Bossa nova came out of late-1950s Rio, when musicians slowed samba down and added cool jazz harmony. Bia Moreno carries that hushed style on by recording beside her apartment window.
input.confidence_reason: The catalog has calm lo-fi, ambient, bossa nova and classical songs plus one track tagged focused, but only 1 or 2 songs per study-friendly genre.
